sections.title: Salary Structure
paragraphs: Employee compensation at Cotelligent is structured as Cost to Company (CTC), which includes Basic Salary, House Rent Allowance (HRA), Special Allowance, Provident Fund (employer contribution), and other benefits.

Basic salary typically constitutes 40-50% of the gross monthly salary. HRA is 50% of basic salary for employees in metro cities (Mumbai, Delhi, Bangalore, Chennai, Kolkata, Hyderabad) and 40% of basic salary for non-metro employees.
Performance bonuses may be paid quarterly or annually depending on the employee's grade and department. Bonus payouts are subject to individual and company performance targets being met.
Sales and client-facing roles may be eligible for incentive-based compensation in addition to fixed salary. The incentive structure is communicated at the time of appointment or promotion.

sections.title: Payroll Processing and Salary Credit
paragraphs: Monthly salaries are processed on the last working day of each calendar month and credited directly to the employee's registered bank account. Any change in bank account details must be submitted to HR at least 10 working days before month end.

Payslips are generated by the 25th of each month and are accessible through the HRMS portal under the Payroll section. Employees are encouraged to review their payslip and report any discrepancies to HR within 5 working days.
Salary revision letters are issued following the annual appraisal cycle, typically in April. The revised salary is effective from April 1st of that financial year unless stated otherwise.
If the last working day falls on a weekend or public holiday, salary will be credited on the preceding working day.

sections.title: Tax Deduction at Source (TDS)
paragraphs: Tax Deducted at Source (TDS) is computed based on the employee's projected annual taxable income and deducted proportionately from each monthly salary. Employees must declare their preferred tax regime (old vs. new) at the beginning of the financial year.

Employees opting for the old tax regime must submit their investment declarations (for exemptions under 80C, 80D, HRA, etc.) at the beginning of the financial year (typically by April 30th). A declaration does not replace actual proof submission.

Investment proofs for the previous financial year must be submitted by February 15th. Failure to submit proofs on time will result in higher TDS deductions in February and March to compensate for any shortfall.
Form 16 (the annual TDS certificate) is issued to all employees by June 15th of the following year. This document is required for filing personal income tax returns.

sections.title: Salary Advances
paragraphs: Employees facing genuine financial emergencies may apply for a salary advance of up to 2 months' basic salary. The advance is interest-free and is recovered in equal monthly installments over a maximum of 6 months.

Salary advance requests must be submitted via the HRMS portal or in writing to HR. Approval requires sign-off from the department head and the Finance department. Only one advance is permitted at a time; a new request can only be made after the previous advance is fully recovered.
Advances will not be granted during the notice period. Pending advances at the time of resignation or termination will be deducted from the full and final settlement.

sections.title: Expense Reimbursement
paragraphs: Employees are reimbursed for pre-approved business expenses including travel, accommodation, client entertainment, and professional subscriptions. All reimbursement claims must include original receipts or invoices.
Expense claims must be submitted within 30 days of incurring the expense. Claims older than 30 days may not be processed without special approval from the Finance head.

Travel reimbursements follow the grade-based travel policy: air travel in economy class for staff and business class for Director level and above for domestic travel exceeding 4 hours. Local travel is reimbursed at actual cost based on fare receipts.

sections.title: Leave Encashment
paragraphs: Employees who separate from the company (through resignation, retirement, or termination) are entitled to encashment of accumulated earned leave balance up to a maximum of 60 days.

Leave encashment is calculated at the rate of basic salary per day (Basic Salary / 26 working days per month). Encashment of earned leave for tax exemption purposes follows the rules under Section 10(10AA) of the Income Tax Act.
Earned leave encashment during the course of employment (without separation) is not permitted except in cases of medical emergency, subject to HR and management approval.
